title: Isolation of Natural Killer (NK) Cells from Human Blood Products
author: Philippa R Kennedy
materials: For experiments with enriched NK cells, PBMCs were processed fresh using negative magnetic bead separation (EasySep Human NK Cell Enrichment Kit; Cat. No:19055, STEMCELL Technologies).

steps.title: Drain Blood Product into Flask
steps.instruction: Drain the blood from the trimacone into a T75 flask containing sterile PBS.

substeps.instruction: Add 40mL 1X sterile PBS to a T75 flask.
Wipe the outside of the trimacone with 70% ethanol.
Cut the bottom tube off at its base and place the trimacone in the mouth of the T75 flask.
Cut the top tube to allow blood to drip into the flask.
If draining is too slow, use a 50mL syringe to force air into the top of the cone.
Rinse the flask with 5mL PBS to collect any remaining blood.

steps.title: Layer Blood onto Ficoll
steps.instruction: Carefully layer the blood/PBS mixture over Ficoll in conical tubes to separate PBMCs.

substeps.instruction: Add 15mL Ficoll (ensure it is less than 3-4 months old) to each 50mL conical tube.
Mix the blood and PBS in the T75 flask using a 25mL serological pipette by pipetting up and down several times.
Slowly and gently pipette 25mL of the blood/PBS mix down the side of the 50mL conical tube at an angle to avoid mixing the layers.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Collect Buffy Coat
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes to separate layers and extract the PBMC-rich buffy coat.

substeps.instruction: Balance tubes using a scale, adding PBS gently if necessary.
Centrifuge at room temperature at 2000rpm (approx. 940g) for 20 minutes with acceleration 5 and no brake.
Carefully remove tubes and optionally pipette off some plasma to better visualize the buffy coat.
Use a sterile transfer pipette/dropper to collect the buffy coat layer into a new 50mL conical tube.

steps.title: Wash the Cells
steps.instruction: Wash the collected buffy coat cells in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Add 20mL PBS to the conical tube containing the buffy coat.
Spin at 2200rpm (750g) for 5 minutes.
If the pellet is loose or cells remain in suspension, vortex the tube, split the suspension between two new 50mL conicals, add 20mL PBS to each, and repeat the spin.
Wash again with PBS.

steps.title: Lyse Red Blood Cells (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform red blood cell lysis if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5-10mL ACK buffer for 3 minutes.
Wash twice with PBS.
Resuspend in 10mL (expected maximum concentration 200 million/ml).

steps.title: Count Nucleated Cells
steps.instruction: Count the PBMCs using a Cellaca (AOPI method) to determine the number of cells.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 25 μL of cells into 475 μL PBS (1/20 dilution).
Mix the dilution 1:1 with AOPI (final dilution 1/40) to reach a measurable range of 1 million/mL to 10 million/mL.

steps.title: Store Excess PBMCs (Optional)
steps.instruction: Freeze excess PBMCs for future use, provided the NK cell proportion is ≥2%.

substeps.instruction: Freeze 100 million PBMCs in 1 mL of 90% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum and 10% DMSO.
Freeze in a styrofoam or controlled temperature cooler (e.g., Mr Frosty) in a -80 °C freezer overnight.
Transfer to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.

steps.title: Recover Cells from Frozen PBMCs
steps.instruction: Thaw and recover frozen PBMCs before enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Thaw cells and wash to remove DMSO.
Culture cells overnight at 4x10^6 /mL in R10 at 37°C and 5% CO2 to allow antigen recovery.

steps.title: Magnetically Enrich NK Cells
steps.instruction: Isolate NK cells using magnetic negative isolation according to manufacturer's instructions.

substeps.instruction: Perform magnetic isolation (preferring purity over yield; pass through the magnet once).
Count cells and verify purity (target 90%-95% CD56+ CD3- cells) via flow cytometry using live/dead, CD56, and CD3 markers.

steps.title: Maintain Cells in Culture
steps.instruction: Maintain PBMCs or enriched NK cells in RPMI 1640 supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin, adding recombinant human IL-15 where specified.
